## At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| **Input** | Frozen airbrushed homogenate (host fraction, ~400 µL) |
| **Output** | SAM concentration (µg mL⁻¹), normalized to protein or surface area |
| **Kit** | BioVision S-Adenosylmethionine (SAM) ELISA kit ([manual](/images/SAM_Kit_Assay.pdf)); Thermo Halt protease inhibitor cocktail |
| **Capacity** | One 96-well plate = 8 standards + 40 samples, in duplicate |
| **Time** | ~1 h sample prep + ~2.5 h assay (estimate) |
| **Tested on** | *Astrangia poculata* |

## Materials

- SAM ELISA kit: pre-coated plate, SAM standard, Standard/Sample dilution buffer, biotin detection antibody + diluent, HRP-streptavidin (SABC) + diluent, wash buffer concentrate, TMB substrate, stop solution, plate sealers
- Protease inhibitor cocktail (Thermo 78430)
- Refrigerated centrifuge, 37 °C incubator, thermocycler or heat block at 37 °C, −80 °C freezer
- Multichannel pipette, plate reader (450 nm)

## Solutions to prepare (per full plate)

| Solution | Recipe |
|---|---|
| **Biotin antibody working solution** (1:100) | 50 µL biotin antibody + 4.95 mL antibody diluent (≥ 4.8 mL needed) |
| **SABC working solution** (1:100) | 100 µL SABC + 9.9 mL SABC diluent (≥ 9.6 mL needed) |
| **1× wash buffer** | 30 mL concentrate + 720 mL DI water. Warm to 40 °C if crystals have formed, then cool to room temp |
| **SAM standards** | Reconstitute the standard in 1 mL Standard/Sample diluent (= 25 µg mL⁻¹), let stand 10 min, mix gently. Make 2-fold serial dilutions (e.g. 0.3 mL standard + 0.3 mL diluent): **25, 12.5, 6.25, 3.125, 1.56, 0.781, 0.39, 0** µg mL⁻¹. Use within 2 h |

## Procedure

### A. Sample preparation

1. Thaw homogenates on ice.
2. Pellet the symbionts: **6,000 × g, 2 min, 4 °C**. Move **400 µL** of supernatant (host) to a new tube.
3. Add protease inhibitor at **1:100** (4 µL to 400 µL) and vortex.
4. Lyse with **5 freeze–thaw cycles**: 5 min at −80 °C → 5 min at 37 °C.
5. Spin **5,000 × g, 5 min** to remove debris. Use the supernatant.

### B. ELISA

6. Bring all reagents, standards and samples to room temperature (30 min).
7. Wash the plate **2×** with 1× wash buffer.
8. Add **50 µL** standard or sample per well, then immediately **50 µL biotin antibody working solution**. Seal, tap gently to mix, and incubate **45 min at 37 °C**.
9. Discard and wash **3×**: fill each well with **350 µL** wash buffer, soak 1–2 min, aspirate. After the last wash, blot the plate upside down on paper towels.
10. Add **100 µL SABC working solution** per well. Seal and incubate **30 min at 37 °C**.
11. Discard and wash **5×** as in step 9.
12. Add **90 µL TMB** per well. Seal and incubate **15–30 min at 37 °C in the dark**, until the first 3–4 standards are visibly blue.
13. Add **50 µL stop solution**. Read at **450 nm within 20 min**.

### C. Calculate

14. Sample and detection antibody go in together, so this is a **competitive** format: signal *decreases* as SAM increases (confirm in the kit manual). Fit a 4-parameter logistic curve to the standards and interpolate the samples. Example script: [SAM.R](https://github.com/kevinhwong1/Astrangia_Nutrition/blob/master/RAnalysis/Scripts/SAM.R).
15. Normalize to protein (from the same homogenate) or to surface area.

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| High background in all wells | Incomplete washing | Soak 1–2 min per wash and blot thoroughly after the last wash |
| Not enough wells for all samples | One plate = 40 samples in duplicate | Choose samples to span treatments and colour range before starting (as in [2019-05-15](../notebook/2019-05-15-sam-elisa-kit-for-a-poculata-nutrition-experiment.md)) |
| Standards don't develop | TMB too cold or incubation too short | Check the blue gradient at 15 min and extend to 30 min if needed |
